1.explanation:
All of the logic and styling for the Calendar lives in this folder:  
1. Calendar.js – this file drives the rendering of the month view, laying out rows and cells expecting CSS Grid to work. IE11 never reaches its fallback and so the cells collapse or overlap.  
2. StyledCalendar.js – the styled-component here is where display: grid, grid-template-rows/columns, and gap are declared. IE11 only supports its old prefixed grid and needs a flex or table fallback.  
3. utils.js – this contains ISO-8601 date parsing (splitting on dashes or feeding strings into new Date(…)). IE11’s Date.parse doesn’t handle yyyy-mm-dd the same way, resulting in NaN/invalid cells.  

By updating StyledCalendar.js to detect Grid.available (or provide a flex fallback) and by normalizing date input in utils.js to an IE-safe parser, the Calendar will render correctly in IE11.
1.bug_scenario: When you load the new Grommet v2 Calendar in IE11 the month-grid completely breaks: the day-cells are mis-positioned or missing, and the numbers themselves are garbled (you can see odd symbols instead of dates). This happens because Calendar is using modern CSS grid without any IE fallback, and it also relies on ISO-8601 date parsing that IE11 does not support natively.

2.explanation:
• StyledCalendar.js defines the calendar’s entire layout using modern CSS Grid properties that IE11 doesn’t understand (e.g. grid‐template‐rows, grid‐template‐columns, grid‐gap). Those rules must be updated or polyfilled (–ms‐grid, explicit ms‐grid‐row/column) to work in IE11.
• Calendar.js is the component that renders the header arrows and day cells into the StyledCalendar wrapper; because the wrapper’s grid CSS is dropped in IE11, its markup collapses and its icons/font‐characters never line up.
• utils.js contains date‐label and formatting logic; while not strictly layout, it supplies the content into StyledCalendar—it’s where you would ensure the right characters/icons are chosen for IE11 environments (or that you’re not inadvertently passing an unsupported icon font).
• Grid.js declares Grid.available and the fallback for older browsers; Calendar does not currently consult that availability check. You could either switch Calendar to use the Grid component (so it falls back automatically in IE11) or copy its availability logic into StyledCalendar.
• webpack.config.babel.js (and the Grommet Babel preset) must be configured with autoprefixer settings (grid: 'autoplace') so that CSS Grid properties are transpiled into –ms‐grid for IE11. Right now those config files are missing or misconfigured, so no prefixes are emitted.
2.bug_scenario: When you open the Grommet Calendar example in IE11, the month view comes up entirely garbled: the day‐of‐week headings and date cells appear as little rectangles or misplaced text, the chevron navigation arrows do not render, and the calendar grid collapses. In modern browsers it uses CSS Grid and renders correctly, but IE11’s incomplete grid support (and lack of –ms‐grid autoprefixing) means the rules in StyledCalendar never take effect, so the calendar falls back to a broken layout.
